selection.provisional_api: raft.RawNode; one serialized event loop per replica; AsyncStorageWrites=false; ReadOnlySafe
selection.transactional_comparator: FoundationDB 7.3.77, Go binding pinned to release commit, API version 730
selection.reason: RawNode provides explicit deterministic message/tick/Ready seams and leaves storage/transport under the embedding boundary. It is an established consensus implementation, not an existing cross-partition transaction engine. FoundationDB supplies the latter and must be compared before choosing the engine.
selection.decision_rule: Choose only after equivalent correctness and durability runs. Hard deployment constraints can disqualify a candidate; measured cost or maintenance risk can justify a tradeoff. No custom consensus protocol and no preference-based dismissal of transactional KV.
selection.limits: This artifact does not certify V2, V3 or a production distributed database. Commands below are the proposed harness interface, not commands already implemented or run.

candidate_adapter_checkpoint.scope: v5/internal/raftlog and v5/internal/replica implement a candidate durable log/RawNode adapter with scoped message/storage and real subprocess fault tests. They are adapter tests, not full V2 acceptance.
full_v2_pending: independent serial-history/cut oracle over the graph contract

pebble_fail_stop_tradeoff.behavior: Fatal WAL commit, MANIFEST and fatal background failure paths invoke Fatalf; the default logger exits the whole embedding process. Not every storage error is fatal: ordinary returned errors must still be propagated.
pebble_fail_stop_tradeoff.adapter_contract: Preserve fail-stop semantics. Do not install a returning/no-op Fatalf logger to pretend a damaged commit pipeline can continue or report success.
pebble_fail_stop_tradeoff.real_subprocess_evidence: Parent independently validated the existing adapter subprocess fault tests in v5/internal/replica/fatal_test.go. Fatal I/O preserves the prior acknowledged prefix on reopen; an interrupted operation remains unknown until recovered. Persistent Create/EIO and ENOSPC reopen faults required supervisor termination after the deadline; tests require the actual injection marker and assert no successful return/packet, then recover the acknowledged prefix. This is adapter-only evidence, not full V2 acceptance.
pebble_fail_stop_tradeoff.selection_obligation: Review process-wide availability impact and restart/recovery requirements against the embedding contract and alternatives before selecting the engine.

validation.source_scope: Parent independently SHA-pinned 49 temporal/state/raftlog/replica files; Raft sources unchanged from reviewed snapshot.
validation.limits: Scoped foundation snapshot, not a consolidated run of the growing v5 module, cross-partition protocol proof, engine selection or V2 completion.

idalloc_checkpoint.source_scope: Eight source/config hashes verified identical to the independently validated snapshot.
idalloc_checkpoint.limits: Primitive checks do not establish allocator integration or distributed ownership correctness; full V1/V2 remain open.

ownership.rho: Database reducers, durable replication adapters, locks/validation, decisions, IDs, ownership fencing, certified cuts, indexes and complete changes.
ownership.embedding_application: Processes, transport and deployment; the spike executable is test support, not a library server or public network API.
ownership.sigma: Reasoning, rule execution, joins, computational frontiers and solvers. Neither comparator executes reasoning inside rho.

verification.method: Primary release pages plus GitHub releases/latest and commits/tag APIs; pinned raw source inspection. Raw tag contents for raft node.go/storage.go and FDB transaction.go were also fetched by immutable commit and matched byte-for-byte.
verification.documentation_drift: Unversioned FoundationDB documentation currently advertises 8.0.0 and developer-guide search results also reference 7.4.7. This evaluation uses 7.3.77 source/docs and does not infer released capabilities from those other documentation versions.
verification.foundationdb_readme_drift: The 7.3.77 Go README still mentions historical C client versions. transaction.go explicitly selects FDB_API_VERSION 730. Verify the actual 7.3.77 native client/headers in the build; do not use the README's old client range as compatibility evidence.
verification.recheck_before_implementation: Refresh releases, vulnerability/license checks and binding build compatibility. Pin checksums and container digests in the executable spike output.

versions.name: FoundationDB
versions.native_requirement: CGO, foundationdb/fdb_c.h and matching libfdb_c client runtime; external fdbserver cluster

versions.name: Pebble catalog candidate
versions.role: Embedded ordered KV catalog/log-storage candidate, not a distributed transaction substitute. Pebble columnar SST blocks do not themselves implement rho's typed temporal graph column API.

versions.name: HashiCorp Raft alternative
versions.assessment: Credible embedded Go consensus alternative with FSM/storage/transport contracts. Still requires rho cross-group transactions and cuts; it does not remove that obligation. RawNode is provisionally favored for deterministic externally driven ticks and Ready ordering in the smallest model/fault harness, not on performance claims.

api_checks: v3.7.0 uses protobuf pointers: RawNode.Step(*raftpb.Message), Ready.Entries []*raftpb.Entry and embedded *raftpb.HardState. Do not copy v3.6 value-based example signatures.
NewRawNode(*raft.Config) (*raft.RawNode,error); Tick(); Propose([]byte) error; HasReady() bool; Ready() raft.Ready; Advance(raft.Ready). RawNode is not thread-safe.

ReadIndex([]byte) yields request-bound ReadStates; wait until the local state machine has applied through that index before answering its authoritative state. A ReadIndex barrier within one group is not a graph cut.

ProposeConfChange(raftpb.ConfChangeI) and ApplyConfChange(raftpb.ConfChangeI) retain membership in snapshots. Use ConfChangeV2/joint consensus for membership changes; bucket ownership transfer is a separate rho protocol.
ReportUnreachable, ReportSnapshot and TransferLeader cover transport feedback and planned failover. TickQuiesced is deprecated and excluded.

obligations: Persist each Ready's entries/hard state/snapshot before outbound messages; honor MustSync. Start with the stricter synchronous path rather than pipelined storage completion messages.
Appending from index i replaces the suffix >=i. Keep entry-term boundary metadata through compaction. Return the library's compacted/unavailable/snapshot-unavailable sentinels correctly.
Advance only after the batch's persistence and application handling completes. Keep returned entries immutable and bound log/cache/Ready/transport byte buffers.

Reopen from stable HardState, ConfState, snapshot and remaining log, with a durable applied checkpoint. The checkpoint never leads graph effects; replay is idempotent after a crash between installation and checkpoint.
MemoryStorage alone is not durable; it can cache/reconstruct a bounded persisted log but cannot justify a durable receipt.
A Raft snapshot must encode rho intents, read/predicate locks, immutable decisions, allocation high-water, floors, epochs, deduplication and retained-cut/feed metadata, not merely current graph rows.

initial_config.resource_limits: Choose finite message, uncommitted-log, inflight and committed-Ready byte limits; include them in results. These timing values are spike settings, not availability promises.
initial_config.lease_based_reads: Excluded from the baseline: correctness must survive arbitrary wall-clock rollback/pause. Logical Tick advances only election/liveness; transaction rounds come from persisted reducer state.

test_seams.name: VFS/stable storage
test_seams.contract: Wrap create/open/write/read/sync/rename/remove/directory-sync and record an operation ordinal. Model volatile bytes separately from synced durable bytes; crash discards the former.
faults: crash between snapshot rename and durable manifest
test_seams.proof: Failed persistence cannot send a durability-dependent Raft reply or produce a rho durable receipt. Corruption fails closed; never fabricate empty state. Real SIGKILL/reopen complements simulated power-loss semantics.

test_seams.name: Clock/scheduler
test_seams.contract: The embedding scheduler drives RawNode.Tick. Inject deterministic tick/event ordering and seeded liveness scheduling; wall time is a separate injected value for metrics/lease expiration.
test_seams.proof: IDs, round fences and safety do not depend on wall clocks or near-simultaneous actions. Liveness is assessed only after restored quorum and fair delivery.

test_seams.name: Network
test_seams.contract: Serialize/own messages in the replica loop, then enqueue immutable frames through application transport. Test transport has explicit deliver/drop/duplicate/reorder/partition/heal operations and bounded bytes.
test_seams.proof: Unknown result stays unknown until durable recovery/dedup resolves it; minority never returns fresh or durable success. Public rho APIs hide Raft/protobuf types.

comparison.embedded_raft: Raft orders one partition; rho must implement recoverable cross-group 2PC plus complete key/predicate locking and decision recovery. Start with coarse partition/range locks for a small exact slice.
comparison.foundationdb: Use one ordinary FDB transaction over both graph key prefixes. Rely on read/write conflict ranges, not a second rho 2PC. Explicitly read invariants/absence and add ranges where required; blind writes and Snapshot() do not validate a read footprint.

comparison.embedded_raft: rho owns MVCC, prepare resolution, fences and retained certificates. Quorum reads and complete installation precede certification.
comparison.foundationdb: Use one fresh read version for the whole ordinary read transaction. Retained rho At(cut), arbitrarily long scans and CDC need an application version/history layer; the bounded native MVCC window is not an indefinitely retained cut. Test paging from retained immutable generations across fresh small transactions.

comparison.embedded_raft: Go consensus core embeds in the application's process with application-provided transport/storage; local one-partition mode can share reducer semantics.
comparison.foundationdb: Go embeds the client, requiring CGO/native client and external fdbserver roles. If the hard requirement is no separate DB server or no native client, this is a deployment disqualification, not proof of bad cost. The plan currently lets the application supply processes: an external runtime must therefore be evaluated explicitly rather than assumed prohibited.

comparison.embedded_raft: Direct typed segments/column pages can derive from the authoritative partition log; catalog/manifest checkpoints must be replay-safe.
comparison.foundationdb: FDB exposes ordered bytes, not rho typed temporal columns. Compare chunked immutable column pages plus a small atomic manifest transaction with row KV as a reference. Upload chunks before publication, bind length/hash/generation, and GC only unreferenced/unpinned generations. Serving local cached files requires a manifest/version completeness check.
comparison.interpretation: The chunk/publication mechanism is a proposed rho layer, not a claimed FDB feature. Do not place all segment bytes in a single transaction.

comparison.embedded_raft: Majority durable acknowledgement must be established by the Ready/VFS integration. A replicated entry in unsynced RAM does not pass.
comparison.foundationdb: FDB commit returns after redundant durable logging under configured redundancy. Verify the deployed triple-redundancy configuration/status and injected failures. Native unknown/cancelled commit results still require a rho request-key/digest record committed with effects.

comparison.embedded_raft: Expose deterministic storage/network/tick seams and independent transaction/cut oracle, then kill six real replica processes and reopen durable files.
comparison.foundationdb: Upstream deterministic simulation is substantial engineering evidence, not proof of our layer. Run actual cluster process/network faults and layer publication/CDC faults. Full upstream simulation requires a source build/Flow workload; do not claim Go client hooks reproduce FDB's internal simulator.

comparison.embedded_raft: Count consensus log, catalog WAL/checkpoints, columns, all three replicas, locks/intents, decision/cut/pin/dedup metadata, replay and application work.
comparison.foundationdb: 7.3.77 documents 10,000-byte keys, 100,000-byte values, 10,000,000-byte affected transaction data and roughly five-second transaction lifetime. Count native client memory plus every server role, duplicated rows/columns, retained history, chunk fetches, retries and publication metadata. Actual bytes/latencies are unmeasured.

comparison.embedded_raft: Compare paged Pebble v2.1.7 with Badger under identical catalog records/cache budgets after removing v4 resident per-row maps. Pebble batches/snapshots/FS seam are useful; none supplies cross-group transactions by itself.
comparison.foundationdb: An embedded local KV is not a fair replacement for FDB distributed transaction guarantees. HashiCorp Raft is another consensus integration candidate, not a transactional-KV equivalent.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Tx touches A/B, coordinator is B, requested scope is A. B durably commits at 120 but A only has a prepare; collect A's applied high-water at 100 and pause B decision lookup.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Fresh A cut must resolve the durable coordinator record or return unavailable; it cannot omit the acknowledged commit. Prepare metadata binds coordinator authority/epoch. After(receipt) includes the same TxID even when coordinator is outside scope.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: Certifying solely from A's applied high-water or ignoring an inaccessible decision must fail the independent oracle.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Validation samples floor 90; enqueue prepare; apply durable fence B=100 before prepare is applied. Also schedule A prepare before fence and B prepare after its fence.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Prepare/fence ordering is authoritative at replicated reducer application. Every post-fence yes vote binds floor >=100 and immutable effect digest; coordinator commits strictly above all voted floors. Stale pre-proposal floor must be raised or the prepare rejected/revalidated.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: A post-fence prepare voting 90 permits a later commit <=100 and invalidates an already published cut. Include delayed local-commit proposals and leader change between fence persistence/application.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Old Tx can decide at 90; fence at 100; decision durable; apply A only; query A/B; kill coordinator leader and replay duplicate resolve messages.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: No undecided eligible prepare remains when certifying. Install every committed local effect <=B atomically with its indexes/postings/history; require certified follower apply positions. A resolved decision without local installation is insufficient.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: Fence-only certification, resolve-only certification and current-index-only historical reads must fail E15/E16/E18.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Freeze A/B, delay one vote, try to add a uniqueness/endpoint participant or reuse TxID with different payload; race recovery abort against a late commit proposal.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Participant set, epochs, request digest and prepared effect digests are immutable before decision. Any discovered extra dependency restarts before prepare. COMMIT requires matching yes votes from every frozen participant; ABORT/COMMIT decisions never change. Timeout alone cannot abort a possibly committed transaction.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: One-participant receipt for a cross-edge, digest mismatch acceptance and conflicting durable decisions must all be rejected.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Pin C, observe endpoint alive/empty unique range/temporal predicate. Concurrent Tx changes it at C+1; historical Tx attempts dependent write. Include a value change and return to original value with a different life/revision.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Acquire the complete current read/predicate footprint and re-evaluate or restart before preparing. Include absent keys, empty ranges, temporal overlap, endpoint LifeIDs, unique keys, topology/catalog/profile dependencies and any history-derived predicate. One immutable old snapshot or current value equality alone cannot validate every such dependency.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: Both write-skew branches, insertion into previously empty range and life ABA must fail if validation ignores those dependencies.

protocol_proof_obligations.case: Locks and conflict serialization across failover
protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Prepare Tx1 with durable key/predicate locks; kill leader; Tx2 overlaps keys/range; recover Tx1 COMMIT or ABORT while delivering duplicate prepare.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Rebuild prepared lock ownership before admitting conflicting work. Priority/TxID order prevents deadlock; bounded retry is explicit. Atomicity tests alone are insufficient: independent serial-history oracle must also reject lost updates, write skew and phantoms.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: Dropping read locks during replay may leave whole transactions atomic but nonserializable; the serial oracle must catch that.

protocol_proof_obligations.case: Ownership transfer, deduplication and retained pins
protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Pin snapshot/feed at C; lose reply to committed request K; fence old bucket; transfer and restart target; replay K and delayed old-epoch write/allocator messages; compact old owner.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Handoff carries retained base/tail, floors, prepared locks/intents and their decisions/coordinator authority, request-key/payload bindings/lease state, allocation high-water, cut/feed pins and lineage. Catalog activation requires durable handoff and epoch fencing. Historical reads and gap-free feed continue or explicitly expire; never silently restart at current state.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: Retry K returns identical result/IDs; different payload under K is rejected. Old owner cannot acknowledge success. Old-cut exact set survives old-owner compaction while the pin remains active.

protocol_proof_obligations.case: Durable ID block reservation and exhaustion
protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Crash immediately before/after quorum reservation, mint part of block, restart allocator, transfer owner and deliver old allocation acknowledgement.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Nonoverlapping graph-qualified opaque 64-bit ranges are durably reserved before issuance. Persist next allocation high-water and allocation authority epoch; do not recycle unused reserved IDs after uncertainty. IDs do not depend on time or placement; exhaustion returns an explicit error.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: No issued ID ever repeats across crash/retry/transfer. Stale authority cannot allocate or commit as current owner.

protocol_proof_obligations.schedule: Collect topology/cut certificate, pause before lease publication, run reaper/segment GC, then return snapshot token; race transfer with feed cursor allocation.
protocol_proof_obligations.required: Durably establish/pin the retained certificate, descriptors, decisions, lineage and feed start before returning success. Reclamation observes those same pins. Expiration does not turn retained reads into partial exact-empty answers.
protocol_proof_obligations.negative_test: A token returned after needed versions/decisions were reclaimed must fail creation rather than succeed and lose history.

executable_spike_plan.command_working_directory: v5/ (the isolated github.com/data-insights-ai/rho-tkg/v5 module); proposed harness/package paths below are relative to that directory
executable_spike_plan.smallest_scope: Integer scalar key/value state plus one cross-partition relationship with two endpoint postings. Use a single coarse lock per partition initially, explicit TxID/request digest, durable ID blocks, a tiny MVCC history, transaction envelopes and cut/pin certificates. No generic graph planner, reasoning executor, large column codec or new consensus algorithm.
proposed_test_support: internal/v5substrate: adapter harness, fault VFS, deterministic scheduler/network, independent serial-history/cut oracle
cmd/v2-substrate-spike: test-only driver/replica modes, filesystem/process/network fault schedules, metrics JSONL
tests/v5substrate: seed/schedule corpus and checked expected failures for P01-P09/E15-E18

embedded_topology.coordinator: Coordinator record lives in one of these two existing groups; do not add an unreplicated coordinator or hidden third group. A scope-only read can have its coordinator in B.
embedded_topology.catalog_and_allocator: For the slice, replicated in A and included in its snapshots; participant epochs validated from pinned catalog state. Measure this service and include A loss in the fault matrix.
embedded_topology.durable_mode: Six separate replica processes, six separate data directories; initially one host for functional crash tests, then three hosts with one A and one B replica on each host for fault-domain/durability and cost runs.
embedded_topology.transfer: Move a bucket A->B while keeping exactly these two three-voter groups; test membership separately using ConfChangeV2 without pretending a seventh voter is part of the fixed baseline.

foundationdb_topology.logical_partitions: Two key prefixes A/B, one native FDB transaction across them
foundationdb_topology.replication: Configure triple redundancy with sufficient independent physical machines and verify config/status before load. The pinned configuration table requires three live machines for progress and at least four machines for fault tolerance (five-plus is recommended), with five ideal coordinators. Three machines holding three copies cannot establish the same one-machine-loss availability as Raft majority-of-three. Record every coordinator, transaction, log and storage role/process.
foundationdb_topology.physical_caveat: FDB dynamically shards storage and separates commit roles. Two prefixes on six workers are not two Raft groups with three replicas. Use at least four independent machines for a one-machine-loss progress comparison, disclose the greater minimum machine count, and report any five-machine recommended configuration separately. Do not hide extra roles; compare declared fault tolerance and total resources.
comparison_modes: immutable chunked columns plus transactional manifest with retained versioning
foundationdb_topology.idempotency: Read request-key/digest record and write result plus all effects/CDC in the same ordinary FDB transaction. Keep callbacks free of external effects because Transact retries. Pre-reserved immutable TxID/IDs remain fixed through retry; accept no duplicate graph effect after unknown commit.

oracle.independence: Represent transactions and exact graph states in a simple separate map/history model. It must not use implementation floor/fence/lock guards as its acceptance rule.
checks: Search for a serial order respecting actual conflict dependencies and acknowledged operation boundaries under the stated consistency mode; do not demand unpromised global real-time round ordering.
At each certified cut compare exact sets of entities, labels/properties, relationship owner and both endpoint postings against entire transaction effects; assert forbidden partial and phantom states.
Historical cut answers remain equal after later writes, index corrections, leader loss, transfer and reopen. Current-state substitution must fail.

Classify unknown outcomes as pending until recovered; distinguish abort, unavailable, expired and exact-empty. Verify complete CDC groups and no snapshot-to-feed gaps/duplicates beyond declared replay.
Delete/reopen endpoint lives and test relationship life masking versus identity-reference observation; no old-edge rebinding.
oracle.existing_reference_limit: design_checks.py explores one already-prepared transaction with atomic decisions. Its 480 schedules/80 certified reads are not Raft, conflict, delayed prepare, failure or transfer validation. Keep it unchanged and add this independent model.

fault_campaign: For every P01-P09 schedule, crash before/after each stable-storage transition; repeat with old/new leader, delayed/reordered/duplicate messages and serializable read/write conflicts.

Process-kill each leader after first prepare, after all prepares before decision, after decision before reply, after A installation before B installation and during snapshot/checkpoint publication; restart from durable directories.

Lose one replica per group, isolate a leader, lose two replicas of a group, kill coordinator quorum and heal. Require explicit unavailable while quorum cannot establish fresh/durable work; require recovery after quorum and fair delivery return.
Exercise VFS sync/rename/ENOSPC faults; SIGKILL alone does not simulate power loss because the OS cache survives. Preserve exact fault traces and durable-image hashes.

FDB: drop client commit reply, kill transaction/storage/log roles, partition fault domains, retry request key, fail chunk upload/manifest publication and race GC/pins. Native transaction internals differ: assert identical external invariants, not fake rho prepare-stage hooks in FDB.

Bound exploratory schedules before random soak: enumerate event orderings for two conflicting transactions, one fence and one transfer; then use fixed recorded seeds. Publish minimal counterexamples with an independent oracle replay.

planned_commands.requires: Implement deterministic adapter/model tests, pinned raft dependency and checked schedules first.
planned_commands.output: Test output plus source/seed/config digest; no disk-latency claims from this simulation.

planned_commands.requires: Implement parent driver spawning exactly six replica child processes with private durable dirs and controlled transport/VFS hooks.
planned_commands.output: Process-kill/restart history, receipts, certificates, oracle outcomes and stable image hashes.

planned_commands.requires: Provision pinned 7.3.77 native client/server, API 730, triple redundancy on at least four independent machines for one-machine-loss progress, status check and role-aware kill/network hooks. Record cluster status before/after.
Pass faults first; populate fixed scalar/cross-edge workload and identical retained-history/index/CDC outputs.
Same facts, predicates, receipts, retention horizon, process-tree resource allowance, fault tolerance and verified disk durability as the raft run.

workloads: cross-edge with endpoint-life and uniqueness checks
late state correction and retained old-cut index scan
transfer under write and retained pins
measurement_matrix.network_profiles: Measure loopback overhead separately; actual three-host LAN then declared injected RTT distributions (1, 20, 100 ms). These RTTs are test settings, not measured WAN links.
report: p50/p95/p99 including retry/wait and failure recovery
disk raw/compressed bytes with replicas, logs, history, columns, indexes and metadata
bytes/fact with source rows and graph facts distinguished
write/read amplification, fsync count/latency, replay tail and open time
measurement_matrix.gate: Zero semantic/durable divergence is mandatory. No performance acceptance threshold is fabricated here; apply V0 consumer targets and the plan's proposed regression/scaling thresholds only after review. Separate exact 2x3 functional evidence from differently shaped FDB deployment cost.

selection_evidence_required: Reproducible source commits/module checksums/native-client and container digests, hardware/filesystem/kernel, role topology, replication and sync policy.
Independent serial/cut oracle passes with preserved histories and seeds, real process-kill/restart results and VFS fault image evidence.
A written deployment verdict distinguishing strict in-process-only constraints from optional application-supplied external processes.
Comparable total cost ledger; historical/cut/CDC/column layers included for both options; no row-only FDB baseline presented as equivalent native columns.
Engine/library selection before format freeze, plus remaining unsupported capabilities and maintenance obligations. A passing simulator or this research artifact alone cannot close V2.
